rules.title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent Coordination
rules.requirement: Owners of residential buildings with six or more units may not use software or services that use nonpublic competitor data to recommend or set rents, lease terms or occupancy levels. Violations are fined $300 per unit per day.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic rent coordination services using nonpublic competitor data; 6+ unit buildings; $300 per unit per day
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential buildings with six or more dwelling units in Cambridge.
rules.penalty: $300 per unit per day; each day is a separate offense
rules.effective_date_note: Section 8.80.040 states the ordinance takes effect March 1, 2027, after the 2026-10-01 query date.
rules.quoted_span: No owner of a residential building containing six or more dwelling units in the City of Cambridge shall use an algorithmic rent coordination service to set rents or occupancy levels for any dwelling unit in such building
rules.review_note: The source document is labeled 'TEST FIXTURE - FICTIONAL', so treat with caution. It is a new local rule and does not amend or replace any existing rule. Pending state bills S.2983 and H.5222 are not law and do not preempt it.
rules.interaction: New local ordinance. It does not amend or replace any existing Cambridge rule. No enacted state algorithmic rent-setting law exists in MA; S.2983 and H.5222 are pending only.

parsed.notes: Only the new document N001 was considered. It supports one rule, Cambridge ch. 8.80, which takes effect 2027-03-01. The document is labeled as a fictional test fixture, so confidence is reduced.
